scope: entire pinned Linux source and behavior; first x86_64 tranche does not reduce this scope
inventory_limitations: Source-family directory inventories and x86 syscall table are complete at their level, but recursive source/Kconfig/driver/UAPI inventories have not been populated.
Directory, file and opcode counts do not measure behavioral completion.
The x32-specific table rows do not include all shared common syscalls; a complete x32 ABI inventory needs both.

initial_repository.source: GitHub API initial snapshot recorded by root audit

completion_rule: A full rewrite can be complete only if inventory_complete=true and all applicable gates and every inventoried obligation have independent evidence for the same exact candidate. NOT_APPLICABLE needs a baseline-specific explanation and cannot remove a feature supported by the pinned baseline.

gates.title: Pinned Linux source, configurations and ABI inventory
gates.acceptance: Enumerate every tracked path, every arch ABI, Kconfig symbol, exported UAPI and driver ID at the fixed commit. Bind the inventory to a full tree digest; no truncated recursive tree accepted.

gates.title: All target kernel implementation in HIA
gates.acceptance: Every executable target section has HIA provenance. No C/Rust/assembly implementation, generated raw-byte payload, hidden interpreter or foreign runtime in the kernel. Host tools are recorded separately.

gates.title: Kernel-capable HIA semantics and backend
gates.acceptance: Verified privilege, exception entry/return, port I/O, MMIO, atomics, fences, SMP ordering, executable/data sections, static storage, address-space access, relocation and freestanding calling-convention support.
gates.verified_subset: single-owner frame allocation and x86-64 emulated boot only

gates.title: Reproducible whole-kernel builds
gates.acceptance: Pin HIA/toolchain/linker inputs, source revision, config, architecture, host tools and artifact hashes. Independently rebuild the exact candidate without network/runtime downloads.
gates.verified_subset: single-owner frame allocation and x86-64 emulated boot only

gates.title: Boot across every baseline architecture and supported platform
gates.acceptance: Firmware/boot protocol entry, mode transition, CPU setup, memory map, page tables, exception recovery and clock initialization verified on declared emulator and hardware matrices.
gates.verified_subset: single-owner frame allocation and x86-64 emulated boot only

gates.title: Complete physical and virtual memory behavior
gates.acceptance: Reserved memory, ownership, allocation/free, page faults, copy-on-write, page cache, reclaim, swap, NUMA, hotplug, OOM, DMA/IOMMU mappings and permissions verified under faults and concurrency.
gates.verified_subset: single-owner frame allocation and x86-64 emulated boot only

gates.title: Task, scheduling and process semantics
gates.acceptance: Preemption, SMP, timers, context switches, FPU/SIMD state, clone/fork/exec/wait, signals, restart semantics, affinity, priorities and accounting verified.

gates.title: Linux user-facing ABI compatibility
gates.acceptance: Every native and compat syscall entry, errno, structure layout, alignment, ioctl, netlink, procfs/sysfs interface and vDSO contract mapped to independent differential tests.

gates.title: VFS and all baseline filesystems
gates.acceptance: Path resolution, permissions, symlinks, rename/unlink, mount namespaces, caches and all filesystem families mapped; persistent filesystems pass crash/durability and corruption checks.

gates.title: Block storage and device paths
gates.acceptance: Discovery, I/O queues, partitions, flush/barrier, discard, hotplug, timeout and error recovery work with real or emulated devices.

gates.title: All baseline networking families
gates.acceptance: Sockets, protocol states, packet parsing, routing, netfilter, namespaces, congestion, checksums, timeouts and hostile-packet tests verified against an independent peer/oracle.

gates.title: All baseline drivers and platform services
gates.acceptance: Driver inventory includes driver/config IDs and hardware IDs, initialization, I/O, shutdown, suspend/resume, DMA, IRQ and failure-recovery acceptance.

gates.title: Security and isolation
gates.acceptance: Credentials, capabilities, LSM, seccomp, namespaces, cgroups, key management and user/kernel separation tested with negative unauthorized-access cases and resource exhaustion.

gates.title: Concurrency correctness
gates.acceptance: Interrupt/SMP races, preemption, lock ordering, RCU, atomics, barriers and device ordering checked using independent litmus/torture tests and documented HIA semantics.

gates.title: Pinned upstream acceptance suites
gates.acceptance: Run selected then complete applicable kselftest and LTP manifests and subsystem suites on reference Linux and HeptaKernel. Preserve all expected IDs, failures, skips, unsupported and timeouts separately.

gates.title: Unmodified Linux workloads
gates.acceptance: Boot a userspace distribution, run unmodified executables and development workloads, exercise persistence/networking/reboot and collect resource/performance/long-duration evidence.

gates.title: Complete rewrite closure
gates.acceptance: All other gates accepted at the same candidate commit; no unresolved source/ABI/architecture/driver obligation; no placeholder/ENOSYS completion credit; independent review and evidence replay.

first_tranche.goal: HIA single-arena frame allocator in x86-64 QEMU
first_tranche.completion_credit: Only this component; none of the complete Linux subsystem gates is closed.
